# Introduction

This document demonstrates several Quarto features that work well when the
primary output is a Microsoft Word (`.docx`) document.

The examples deliberately avoid Jupyter, Python, and notebook execution.
Code blocks are rendered as source code rather than executed.

# Code Blocks

## Option 1 — Plain Code Block

A simple fenced code block is the most portable option for DOCX output.

```text
TestExecution
  ├── Initialize
  ├── Execute tests
  ├── Collect results
  └── Generate report
```

## Option 2 — Language-Specific Code Block

A language can be specified to enable syntax highlighting.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

echo "Starting test execution"

./run_tests.sh \
  --suite regression \
  --log-level INFO \
  --output results/
```

The code is displayed in the document; it is not executed by Quarto.

## Option 3 — Code Block with Caption and Reference

A code block can have a caption and identifier.

```yaml
test_execution:
  environment: test
  suite: regression
  retries: 3
  logging:
    level: INFO
    output: results/execution.log
```

: Example test execution configuration {#lst-config}

The configuration shown in Listing @lst-config is suitable for a simple
execution-control file.

# Schemas and Diagrams

## Example 1 — Mermaid Flowchart

Mermaid can be used for a process flow.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Start Test Execution] --> B[Load Configuration]
    B --> C[Initialize Environment]
    C --> D[Execute Tests]
    D --> E[Collect Results]
    E --> F[Generate Report]
    F --> G[Finish]
```

: Test execution flow {#fig-flow}

The flow in Figure @fig-flow illustrates the high-level execution lifecycle.

## Example 2 — Mermaid Sequence Diagram

A sequence diagram is useful for showing interactions between components.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner
    participant DUT as Device Under Test
    participant Logger
    participant Reporter

    Runner->>DUT: Start test
    DUT-->>Runner: Test result
    Runner->>Logger: Write execution event
    Logger-->>Runner: Event stored
    Runner->>Reporter: Generate report
    Reporter-->>Runner: Report ready
```

: Test execution interaction sequence {#fig-sequence}

## Example 3 — Mermaid Entity Relationship Diagram

An ER diagram can describe the logical data model.

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
    TEST_RUN ||--o{ TEST_CASE : contains
    TEST_CASE ||--o{ TEST_RESULT : produces
    TEST_RUN ||--|| EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT : uses

    TEST_RUN {
        string run_id
        datetime started_at
        string status
    }

    TEST_CASE {
        string test_id
        string name
        string suite
    }

    TEST_RESULT {
        string result_id
        string status
        string log_reference
    }

    EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT {
        string environment_id
        string name
        string version
    }
```

: Logical test execution data model {#fig-er}

## Example 4 — Mermaid State Diagram

State diagrams are useful when an object or execution moves through
well-defined states.

```{mermaid}
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Created
    Created --> Queued
    Queued --> Running
    Running --> Passed
    Running --> Failed
    Running --> Aborted
    Failed --> Retrying
    Retrying --> Running
    Passed --> Completed
    Aborted --> Completed
    Completed --> [*]
```

: Test run state lifecycle {#fig-state}

## Example 5 — Mermaid Class Diagram

A class diagram can document the structure of a test automation model.

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class TestRun {
        +String runId
        +DateTime startedAt
        +String status
        +start()
        +finish()
    }

    class TestCase {
        +String testId
        +String name
        +execute()
    }

    class TestResult {
        +String status
        +String message
        +String logPath
    }

    TestRun "1" --> "*" TestCase : executes
    TestCase "1" --> "*" TestResult : produces
```

: Test automation object model {#fig-class}

# DOCX Notes

The examples in this document are intentionally based on features that can
be processed without Jupyter.

For a DOCX-oriented Quarto project, a typical command is:

```bash
quarto render examples.qmd --to docx
```

If Mermaid rendering is unavailable in the local Quarto installation,
install or enable the Mermaid rendering support appropriate for the Quarto
version being used.

# Summary

This example contains:

1. Two different table layouts.
2. Three different code-block approaches.
3. Five different schema/diagram examples:
   - Flowchart
   - Sequence diagram
   - Entity-relationship diagram
   - State diagram
   - Class diagram

The document is designed as a starting point for a larger DOCX-based
technical document.
